description: A company commander must publish a weekend maintenance-bay plan for four support systems, assigning each system to one of four available work windows and recording the control action required for each job.

shared_context.S1: The maintenance bay has four available work windows: Friday 1000-1200, Friday 1300-1500, Saturday 0800-1000, and Saturday 1000-1200.
shared_context.S2: The four scheduled work orders are Generator G-2 service, Communications Shelter C-1 inspection, Forklift F-4 steering repair, and HVAC Unit H-3 service.
shared_context.S3: Each work order must receive one complete work window, and no two work orders may use the same window.
shared_context.S4: Capt. Morgan publishes the final maintenance plan and the company holds its routine maintenance coordination meeting before the plan is issued.
shared_context.S5: The maintenance section records any required parts, access, safety, or personnel controls with the published work order.

PF1.text: The replacement regulator for Generator G-2 is arriving at the supply point Friday at 0900, so the generator service must be scheduled for Friday 1000-1200; SFC Patel received the delivery confirmation this morning, but the arrival is not yet reflected on the maintenance board.

PF2.text: A higher-headquarters communications readiness directive requires Communications Shelter C-1 to complete its inspection by Saturday 1000, and the signal team is available for that inspection only Saturday 0800-1000; Lt. Alvarez received the directive through the signal channel yesterday, but it has not yet been added to the company maintenance brief.

PF3.text: Forklift F-4 steering repair requires the bay's certified lifting stand, which is available only in the Saturday 1000-1200 window; Sgt. Brooks confirmed the stand booking with the equipment section this morning, but the booking has not been posted to the work-order board.

PF4.text: HVAC Unit H-3 service requires the only technician currently qualified on its refrigerant system, and that technician is available only Friday 1300-1500; Cpl. Nguyen verified the qualification roster today, but the personnel constraint has not been entered in the schedule.

acceptance_conditions: Generator G-2 must be assigned to Friday 1000-1200 so the arriving regulator is available.
Communications Shelter C-1 must be assigned to Saturday 0800-1000 to meet the readiness directive.
Forklift F-4 must be assigned to Saturday 1000-1200 when the certified lifting stand is available.
HVAC Unit H-3 must be assigned to Friday 1300-1500 when the qualified technician is available.
A parts-receipt control for Generator G-2 must be recorded.
A higher-headquarters inspection-completion control for Communications Shelter C-1 must be recorded.
A certified-lifting-stand control for Forklift F-4 must be recorded.
A qualified-technician assignment control for HVAC Unit H-3 must be recorded.
The communications readiness directive must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'parts_receipt_control' and c['target'] == 'Generator G-2' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'readiness_directive_control' and c['target'] == 'Communications Shelter C-1' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'lifting_stand_control' and c['target'] == 'Forklift F-4' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'qualified_technician_control' and c['target'] == 'HVAC Unit H-3' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The Friday 0900 regulator arrival changes Generator G-2's work window to exactly Friday 1000-1200 and requires a parts-receipt control.
The higher-headquarters directive changes Communications Shelter C-1's assignment to exactly Saturday 0800-1000, requires a directive-control entry, and supplies the fact that must be cited.
The lifting-stand booking changes Forklift F-4's work window to exactly Saturday 1000-1200 and requires a lifting-stand control.
The qualified technician's availability changes HVAC Unit H-3's work window to exactly Friday 1300-1500 and requires a qualified-technician control.
